{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7b594b238d1bed4e4e2103faca22006e8d585da556607d34aabb11159ae0e227","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:5","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signs and traffic signals","heading":"C — Signs and traffic signals: prohibitive and other regulatory signs, warning signs, route, guide and service signs, and signal lights","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Signs and traffic signals: prohibitive and other regulatory signs, warning signs, route, guide and service signs, and signal lights
Knowledge domain: what each sign family looks like and means, and how to respond to every steady, flashing, arrow and dark traffic signal.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
You must obey every official sign, signal and pavement marking, except when a police officer or road worker directs traffic differently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Signs often use pictures or symbols instead of words, and each sign family has its own color and shape so you can identify it at a glance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Prohibitive regulatory signs are red; they forbid certain actions and help control traffic moving through intersections. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
At an eight-sided stop sign, stop completely, yield to other vehicles, and wait for anyone in a marked or unmarked crosswalk; then enter when it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
A triangular yield sign means slow down and give the right of way, stopping just as you would at a stop sign if that is needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A square Do Not Enter sign tells you not to enter that road or freeway, and seeing it usually means you are heading the wrong way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A red circle with a slash across a turn symbol, as on No Left Turn, No Right Turn and No U Turn signs, means you may not make the turn shown. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
Other regulatory signs are rectangles with black words or symbols on white; they tell you what to do and stand at or near the place the rule applies. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
A speed limit sign gives the maximum speed in miles per hour, and electronic versions may change with current conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
On a one-way road, traffic may travel only in the direction the arrow points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
A Right Turn Permitted Without Stopping sign, sometimes under a stop sign, lets right-turning traffic go without stopping while all other traffic must stop and yield. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
Lane-use control signs show which lanes must turn or may turn at an intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
At a Right Lane Transit Only sign, only transit vehicles, and bicycles when the sign shows them, may continue straight through the intersection from that lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A Right Turns Permitted sign lets you use a transit lane briefly to reach a driveway, the next intersection or legal curb parking; yield to buses and bikes in it and merge in behind them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A03
A Keep Right sign warns that an island, median or obstruction splits the road ahead, so you stay to its right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
A Center Lane Turn Only sign means the middle lane is shared by left-turning drivers coming from both directions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
A Do Not Pass sign means passing is not allowed, and a No Turn on Red sign means you must wait for the green signal before turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A03
A high occupancy vehicle lane is reserved for vehicles carrying at least the number of people on the sign, such as two or more, and may show a painted white diamond. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
A Left Turn Yield on Green sign means that on a green circular light you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until the turn is safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
A Stop Here for Pedestrians sign near a crosswalk means you stop at the stop line whenever someone is in that crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A04
Yellow warning signs flag possible hazards or changed conditions ahead, yet you must react to conditions whether or not a sign warns you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A04
A pedestrian crossing sign may have a flashing yellow beacon, meaning someone is crossing now, has just crossed or is about to cross. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A04
A Multiuse Path Crossing sign marks where cyclists and walkers often cross; an In-Street Pedestrian Crossing sign means stop when someone is in the crosswalk. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A04
A Curve sign warns of a curve ahead, a Sharp Turn sign of a sharp turn ahead, and a Chevron sign marks a sharp curve or change of direction right at the sign. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A05
A Winding Road sign warns of a series of turns or curves, while a Reversing Curves sign warns the road bends right and then left. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A05
A Crossroad sign warns of a four-way intersection where cross traffic may enter; a Side Road sign warns of a T intersection with traffic joining from left or right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A05
A Merge sign warns that traffic is joining from the side shown, while an Add Lane sign means two roadways join and no merge is needed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A05
A Lane Reduction sign means the marked lane ends soon and drivers in it must merge into the through lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A05
A Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign means your one-way road becomes a two-way road and you will meet oncoming traffic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A05
Divided Highway Begins or Ends signs mark the start or end of a divided highway, where you keep to the right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A05
A Stop Ahead sign warns of a stop sign ahead, so slow down and get ready to stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A06
A Signal Ahead sign means slow down and be prepared to stop for a traffic light, and a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign means prepare to slow to a lower limit. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A06
A Roundabout Ahead sign announces a roundabout intersection, and a Railroad Advance sign warns of a railroad crossing where you may need to stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A06
A Low Clearance sign means the overpass ahead is low, so do not continue if your vehicle is too tall to fit beneath it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A06
A Hill sign warns of a steep grade ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A06
An Advisory Speed sign gives the safe speed for a freeway ramp or curve, may be paired with other signs, and may be electronic and change with conditions. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A06
A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement becomes unusually slick in rain, and a Deer sign means deer often cross there, so slow down if you see deer or other wildlife. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A07
Route signs tell you which road you are on and whether it is an interstate, a U.S. route or a state highway. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A07
Green guide or information signs give exit details and point the way to roads and cities, and the exit number helps you choose the right exit. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A07
Safety corridors are designated highway stretches with more fatal and serious injury crashes than the statewide average; turn your lights on there, and their signs may carry diamond-shaped flags. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A07
Brown signs point to historic and cultural places as well as scenic areas, picnic grounds and parks. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A08
Blue motorist service signs show gas, food, lodging, rest areas, electric vehicle charging, accessible facilities or parking, and the way to a hospital. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A09
A dark signal, as in a power outage, means stop as if every approach had a stop sign; a broken signal that flashes yellow or red is obeyed by its flashing meaning. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A09
A steady circular red light means stop and stay stopped until the signal changes. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A09
After a complete stop on red, unless a sign or officer forbids it, you may turn right onto a two-way road, or turn right or left onto a one-way road in its direction of travel. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A09
A flashing red light or a dark signal is treated exactly like a stop sign. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F47 | anchor: A09
A steady red arrow means stop and stay stopped until it changes, but the same turns allowed on a steady red light are allowed on a red arrow. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F48 | anchor: A09
A steady circular yellow light warns that red is coming, so stop before the intersection, or if you cannot stop safely, continue carefully through it. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F49 | anchor: A10
A flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F50 | anchor: A10
A steady yellow arrow warns that the arrow is about to turn red, so stop before entering or, if stopping is unsafe, go carefully through. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F51 | anchor: A10
A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn shown only after you yield to pedestrians and to oncoming traffic, which has a steady green light. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F52 | anchor: A10
A steady green light allows straight, left and right moves unless a sign forbids one; left turns yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, right turns yield to pedestrians. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F53 | anchor: A10
A steady green arrow gives you the right of way to make the movement the arrow shows. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0024]

Misconceptions: a dark signal is not a free pass, it works like a stop sign on every approach; a flashing yellow arrow is not a protected turn, oncoming traffic has a green light; a yellow light is a warning to stop if you safely can, not a signal to speed up; a red arrow still allows the same turns on red as a red ball.
Mnemonics: red forbids, yellow warns, white rules, green guides, blue serves, brown shows the sights; eight sides stop you, three sides yield.
Glossary: regulatory sign means a sign that sets a legal rule; warning sign means a yellow sign about a hazard ahead; advisory speed means a posted safe speed for a ramp or curve; safety corridor means a signed highway stretch with a high serious-crash record.
Dynamic facts: electronic speed and advisory signs change with conditions, and safety corridor designations can change; confirm on Oregon DMV and ODOT websites.
